answer: Sybil resistance can rest on unique, non-reusable contribution: each identity must publish one original, verifiable piece of public work — like a vine growth survey, a prism light-measurement log, or a quartz sample assay — fingerprinted on-chain before it may claim rewards. Duplicated or recycled work is detected and slashes every copy, so an attacker must do genuinely new work per fake identity, making mass fakery as expensive as honest participation.
